public_body: Fall River Board Of Park Commissioners
overall: The AG found the Park Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely file member certifications for a 2018 appointment and 2020 reappointments, ordered compliance and one overdue certification, declined the Traffic Board issue, and rejected a civil penalty.

allegations.summary: A commissioner appointed to the board in 2018 did not sign an Open Meeting Law certification for this board, relying on an older certification filed for a different board.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the fact that Commissioner Rego had a two-year-old certification on file relating to her appointment to a different public body does not absolve her of the obligation to sign a certification in her capacity as a member of this Board.

allegations.summary: Three commissioners reappointed in 2020 allegedly did not complete the required Open Meeting Law certifications within two weeks of reappointment.
allegations.key_passage: we find that all three commissioners violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to complete the required certifications within two weeks of reappointment.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised timeliness of a commissioner's certification for appointment to a separate city traffic board, a different public body.
allegations.key_passage: This complaint was filed with the Board of Park Commissioners only and we therefore decline to review any allegations pertaining to a separate public body.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
A commissioner who had not yet certified must complete the certification form and file it with the City Clerk within 30 days of the letter.
remedy_passage: Therefore, we order Commissioner Farias to complete the certification form and file it with the City Clerk within 30 days of the date of this letter.
